sources.entry: Book Factory by Robert Guss - A comprehensive pipeline of Skills that replicates traditional publishing infrastructure for nonfiction book creation using specialized Claude skills.

summary.one_liner: A personal Claude Code and Claude.ai toolkit of skills, hooks, and templates, including a non-fiction book-writing pipeline (non-fiction-book-factory).
summary.what_it_does: The repository bundles packaged workflows ("skills") that Claude follows when invoked, covering brainstorming, session handoffs, leading a project with worker agents, project wikis, iOS app-store opportunity research, and book/writing work. The README lists a book section with ebook-factory (a focused ebook pipeline), non-fiction-book-factory (a full pipeline from idea to chapter architecture), and writing (voice capture and ghost writing). It also provides hooks, shell scripts tied to Claude Code events: auto-format on PostToolUse (ruff, goimports, prettier), change-summary on Stop (TypeScript checking and session summary), and compaction on PreCompact. Templates include HUMAN.md, CLAUDE.md, and a compaction strategy document. A build.py script packages a skill as a .skill file for upload to Claude.ai. The README does not describe the internal steps of the book factory pipeline beyond the one-line summary.
use_cases: Structure a nonfiction book from idea to chapter outline
Ghost-write or capture a personal writing voice
Hand off work context between Claude sessions
Auto-format code after edits in Claude Code
Package a skill for upload to Claude.ai
how_to_run: git clone the repository (URL not given in the README)
notable: Book-writing skills (ebook-factory, non-fiction-book-factory, writing) sit alongside coding and research skills in one toolkit
Skills work in both Claude Code CLI (via CLAUDE.md references) and Claude.ai (via packaged .skill files)
Hooks are event-driven shell scripts for PostToolUse, Stop, and PreCompact
project-wiki skill described as a Karpathy-style LLM wiki published with Quartz
lead skill sends briefs to fresh Opus workers in Herdr
caveats: The README does not give a git clone URL; the clone command is incomplete
The book factory pipeline is described only in one line; its internal stages are not documented in the README
Full documentation is linked externally (Getting Started, All Skills, Developer Guide) and was not included
Some skills depend on external tools named in the README (Herdr, Quartz, just, uv)
